data.narrative:
Planet Labs is a publicly traded Space & Aerospace company founded by Chris Boshuizen, William Marshall, and Robbie Schingler. The valuation universe comprises 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including Rocket Lab, Firefly Aerospace, Astroscale, SpaceX, and ICEYE.

The peer-median method is the applicable triangulation approach, drawing from three same-sector, same-stage comparables: Rocket Lab ($40.0B), Firefly Aerospace ($2.9B), and Astroscale ($840M). The median valuation across this cohort is $2.9B, establishing the central estimate. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples—the sector median stands at 27.4x across six public tickers—cannot be applied absent Planet Labs' disclosed revenue figures. Revenue disclosure remains uncommon among private companies and is absent from available data here.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $2.5B to $3.3B, centered on $2.9B. This range reflects the inherent dispersion within the peer set, where valuations span from $840M to $40.0B. The current public-market valuation of $7.56B sits materially above the peer-median estimate, a divergence that warrants scrutiny of idiosyncratic factors—execution track record, revenue trajectory, or market positioning—not captured in the comparable set. The primary uncertainty stems from the wide valuation spread among peers and the absence of revenue-based anchoring.
